background.text: And finally, what do you say to those people who call in right into our show and who don't believe Hillary is trustable? And, you know, that is basically what motivates them to vote for Donald Trump.

I want somebody who has worked on military issues, not somebody who says the military is a disaster, which Donald Trump says, who attacks John McCain, says he can't be a hero because he was a POW, attacks a gold star family. background.text: All right. I want to shift to guns. This was a big topic, obviously, in both chambers of Congress this week. You've said this on the Heller decision. You've said that you strongly believe that there is an individual right, and you completely accept the Heller decision that says the right is individual, which means you cannot essentially prevent many individuals from whatever it is, concealing carry and buying certain weapons. So what room is there to regulate? Do you believe the person that you can regulate, the individual, or that you regulate the firearm?

ground_truth: Yeah, great question. So, there is an individual right, but the right says well-regulated. In the Second Amendment is the phrase well-regulated. Let's talk about the First Amendment for a second. Freedom of speech. We believe it. You're a journalist, but you can't libel or slander somebody with no consequence. I can't take classified information I get as a senator and give it to somebody with no consequence. Freedom of speech has reasonable limits. Freedom of assembly. We can protest, but you can't march onto the floor of the Senate and do crazy stuff. No, there's going to be rules and regulations. And the Second Amendment is exactly the same. It says well-regulated in the amendment. And the Heller case said, sure, it's an individual right, but there's reasonable regulation. And the court has upheld, the courts, you know, for many years have upheld all.
